Click *Throw the ball*: the ball leaves the centre towards a friend on the rim. The left disc shows its path seen from space, the right disc as the riders see it. *Northern hemisphere ↺* and *Southern hemisphere ↻* set the direction in which the merry-go-round turns, *Spin* its speed.

::: {.column-page}
{{< geores sim="coriolis" >}}
:::

## What to look for

- Seen from space, does the ball curve? Why does it still miss the friend?
- Seen by the riders, which way does the ball curve in the northern hemisphere? And in the southern hemisphere?
- Turn *Spin* up and throw again: how does the curve change?
- Seen from above the North Pole, the Earth turns anticlockwise, like the merry-go-round ↺. Which way are winds deflected in the northern hemisphere?

## How it works

Seen from space, the ball flies in a straight line at a constant speed. The riders' view is the same path, turned back by the angle the merry-go-round has turned during the flight. The merry-go-round stands for the Earth seen from above a pole: anticlockwise above the North Pole, clockwise above the South Pole. A flat disc does not show that on the Earth the deflection is strongest near the poles and disappears at the equator.
